q: The Knill–Laflamme conditions for quantum error correction state that a code C corrects errors {Eₖ} iff:
opts: The errors map C to orthogonal subspaces
⟨ψ|Eₖ†El|φ⟩ = cₖₗ⟨ψ|φ⟩ for all |ψ⟩,|φ⟩ ∈ C (errors act uniformly on the code)
∑ₖ Eₖ†Eₖ = I (errors form a CPTP map)
The code has minimum distance d ≥ 2t+1 for t-error correction
exp: Knill–Laflamme: the errors cannot distinguish states within the code — they act proportionally on all code states. This means no information about the encoded logical state leaks into which error occurred, allowing perfect recovery.
